**B**

Both summaries are accurate, cover the same content, and land at roughly 125–130 words. Neither strictly meets the 120-word limit, so length doesn't separate them. B is better because of how it uses those words for a busy manager.

1. **Order:** B puts the only action item first. A buries it at the end, after a line saying "No action is needed for most customers," which a skimming reader may take as permission to stop.
2. **Usefulness of the action item:** B gives what's needed to act or delegate: the menu path (Admin > Integrations > Payroll (v1)), the business consequence (staff could be paid late), and the help-centre guide. A says only that timesheets "will stop reaching payroll," which undersells the risk.
3. **Brevity elsewhere:** B condenses the improvements and fixes into one "Also" line, keeping the weight on what matters.

Both have a minor flaw: B labels the new features "automatic," and A implies the same. In fact, area-based swap approvals need setup in Admin > Permissions > Areas.
